newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania's founding father celebrates 75th birthday.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania's founding father celebrates 75th birthday.

text.p: Tanzania's socialist founding father, Julius Nyerere, told more than 1,000 well-wishers on his 75th birthday on Sunday he was privileged to reach old age.
"In the North it is now normal -- in the South it is a privilege to reach my age. This is wrong," the former president and international statesman said.
Nyerere was partly responsible for the coinage of the terms North and South, to describe the wealthy and poor parts of the globe respectively.

Tanzania's current President Benjamin Mkapa, Organisation of African Unity (OAU) secretary-general and fellow-Tanzanian Salim Ahmed Salim, Zanzibar President Salmin Amour and former Tanzanian president Ali Hassan Mwinyi were among guests at Nyerere's birthday party in Dar es Salaam.
Mwinyi succeeded Nyerere when he retired from the presidency in 1985, having led the country since independence in 1961.
Dressed in a dark safari-style suit Nyerere was in exuberant mood at Sunday's ceremony. His speech was broadcast live on national television.

Widely hailed for his statesmanship, Nyerere has also been criticised for making Tanzania a hardline socialist state -- with nationalisation of private property and forcing millions of peasants into collective villages -- in 1967.

Nyerere has since admitted that mistakes were made in the turn to socialism, which led to the collapse of key sectors of the economy, such as the formerly booming sisal trade. Tanzania is now reviving private enterprise -- with favourable effects on the economy.
